plan.chapterName: OpenStax Precalculus 2e, chapter 4: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
plan.contextChunk: This figure presents a single labeled sketch of a logistic growth curve on unscaled axes: a horizontal axis labeled t and a vertical axis labeled f(t), both double-arrowed and carrying no numeric ticks. A dashed orange horizontal line stretches across the upper part of the plot, tagged y = c at its left end and joined by a black leader to the annotation Carrying capacity. The solid dark blue curve enters from the lower left, crosses the vertical axis at a marked point labeled (0, c/(1 + a)) and identified as the Initial value of population, steepens through the middle of the frame, then flattens and runs rightward just beneath the dashed line without meeting it. A filled dot on the steepest part of the rise is labeled with the coordinates (ln(a)/b, c/2) and connected by a leader to the words Point of maximum growth. The curve's formula, f(t) = c/(1 + ae^(-bx)), is printed in blue to the right of the upper bend. The three annotations single out what the reader is meant to take from the shape: where the curve starts, where its slope is greatest, and the ceiling it approaches. Together they establish that growth of this kind accelerates only until the population reaches half the carrying capacity, after which the rate of increase falls away as the curve saturates.

interactionPlan.concept: A logistic curve f(t) = c/(1 + ae^(-bx)) starts at c/(1+a), grows fastest at half the carrying capacity c/2 (at t = ln(a)/b), and then saturates toward the ceiling y = c; the growth rate b controls how steep and how early that transition happens.
elements: horizontal axis labeled t, double-arrowed, no numeric ticks
vertical axis labeled f(t), double-arrowed, no numeric ticks
solid dark blue logistic curve entering low at left, steepening through the middle, flattening rightward beneath the asymptote
dashed orange horizontal asymptote line, tagged 'y = c' in orange at its left end
annotation 'Carrying capacity' with black leader arrow to the dashed line
formula label 'f(t) = c / (1 + ae^(-bx))' in blue near the upper bend
filled inflection dot labeled (ln(a)/b, c/2) with leader 'Point of maximum growth'
filled intercept dot at the vertical axis labeled (0, c/(1+a)) with leader 'Initial value of population'
draggable time marker on the curve (from t slider)
tangent line at the time marker, visually showing current slope
vertical gap indicator from the time marker up to the dashed y = c line
readout panel showing current t, population f(t), tangent slope, and remaining distance to c

interactions.label: Time t
interactions.teaches: Sweeping t along the curve shows the tangent slope rise until f(t) passes c/2 and then fall, while the gap to y = c shrinks — growth is fastest exactly at half the carrying capacity and slows as saturation nears

interactions.label: Growth rate b
interactions.teaches: Increasing b steepens the S-curve and moves the maximum-growth point left (t = ln(a)/b shrinks), while decreasing b flattens the transition and pushes it later — b controls the timing and intensity of the approach to saturation

demo_steps.title: Start and ceiling
demo_steps.narration: At t = 0 the marker sits on the intercept (0, c/(1+a)), the initial population, and the dashed line y = c marks the carrying capacity the curve never reaches.

demo_steps.title: Where growth is fastest
demo_steps.narration: Drag t rightward until the population reaches c/2: the tangent is steepest here, at t = ln(a)/b, the point of maximum growth. Past it, the slope shrinks and the gap to y = c closes.

demo_steps.title: Effect of growth rate b
demo_steps.narration: Increase b and the S-curve steepens while the maximum-growth point shifts left; decrease b and the whole transition stretches out — same ceiling c, different pace.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Logistic growth accelerates only until the population reaches half the carrying capacity; from then on the slope falls and the curve saturates toward y = c, with b setting how quickly that turnaround arrives.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Unscaled axes with arrowheads both ways, labels t (horizontal) and f(t) (vertical). Dashed orange asymptote across the top with 'y = c' in orange at its left end and a 'Carrying capacity' leader arrow. Dark blue logistic curve plotted over roughly t ∈ [-6, 10] with defaults a = 5, b = 1 so the intercept 5/6 and inflection at (ln 5, c/2) ≈ (1.6, 0.5) sit right of the axis as in the figure. Formula text in blue beside the upper bend. When the time slider moves, draw a filled marker on the curve with a short tangent segment and a dashed vertical gap line up to y = c; a small readout shows t, f(t), slope, and gap. When b changes, redraw the curve and move the inflection annotation (ln(a)/b, c/2) accordingly; intercept and asymptote stay fixed.

plan.authoredInteractions:

authoredContext:
The graph in the figure shows how the growth rate changes over time. The graph increases from left to right, but the growth rate only increases until it reaches its point of maximum growth rate, at which point the rate of increase decreases.

Graph of f(t)=c/(1+ae^(-tx)). The carrying capacity is the asymptote at y=c. The initial value of population is (0, c/(1+a)). The point of maximum growth is (ln(a)/b, c/2).

discrepancies: the source formula is rendered as a stacked fraction f(t) = c/(1 + a e^(−bx)); the generated version shows inline plain text 'f(t) = c / (1 + a e^(−bx))'
extra red tangent segment and gray dashed 'gap to c' line are drawn at the default state; neither appears in the source figure

in the source the intercept dot and label (0, c/(1+a)) sit noticeably above the t-axis on the y-axis; in the generated figure the curve's lower tail and intercept sit very close to the axis, flattening the S-curve's left portion
source axes carry small tick-like arrows only at positive ends with the y-axis at the left; the generated figure draws double arrowheads on both axes, adding arrowheads the source lacks
evaluation.notes: A faithful, well-annotated logistic-growth figure with correct asymptote, inflection and intercept labels, plus genuinely useful t and b sliders and a working 3-step demo; minor issues are the inline (non-fraction) formula rendering, extra tangent/gap lines not in the source, and a slightly compressed lower tail near the axis.
action_items: Render the formula as a stacked fraction (c over 1 + a e^(−bx)) to match the source typography, or at minimum use 'ae^(−bx)' without the redundant space.
Hide the red tangent segment and gray gap line at step 0 so the default state matches the static source; reveal them only when the time slider moves or in later demo steps.
Raise the y-axis minimum margin or shift the view so the intercept (0, c/(1+a)) is visibly above the t-axis, restoring the S-curve's lifted lower tail.
Remove the extra leftward/downward arrowheads on the axes to match the source's single-direction arrows.
